related.text: The lean thread computed a neutral substitution budget for this family from a machine-checked Kimura fixation-probability theorem and the family’s 48–56 Ma fossil range, and reached an explicit "inconclusive": the adaptive floor needs a favored-mutation rate nobody has defined, and "the substitutions a wing requires" is not a defined quantity, so there is nothing to compare it against.
related.relation: Two independent statements about the same taxon, cited in one direction only. Neither supports or derives from the other, and neither is evidence about the transition Darwin imagined.

related.text: The lean thread put this file through a proof kernel and certified that the structure is well-formed under its own rules: 536 distinct terms, 674 part_of edges, every term reaching the body root, and the per-level counts matching what this page claims. Acyclicity there is not tested but proved, from the level function alone: every edge goes strictly down a level, so no path can return to where it started, and the 114 terms sitting under more than one parent are converging paths rather than loops. Two deliberately sabotaged copies are rejected. Recounted here independently against the same file with the same result — after a naive walk-up of my own first reported 106 cycles that are not there, which is the mistake the level-function argument rules out by construction.
related.relation: This certifies the shape of the artifact, not the biology. A well-formed tree built on mistaken ontology statements would pass, and the certificate says so: it assumes Uberon, the Cell Ontology and Ubergraph are right, and claims nothing about any fish being real. It is therefore cited here rather than attached as evidence for the blueprint.

claim.statement: For neutral mutations the long-run rate of molecular substitution equals the mutation rate per generation, independent of population size, which yields a molecular clock.
claim.work: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level

attachments.why_this_protein: Cytochrome c is the protein on which the molecular clock was first read (Margoliash 1963; Zuckerkandl and Pauling 1965; Fitch and Margoliash 1967): its amino-acid differences between species grow with divergence time while the protein keeps doing the same job. Folding orthologs from cattle, tuna and yeast with the same model shows what the clock's substitutions do to the predicted fold.

what_this_does_and_does_not_show: It shows that a hosted ESMFold service can be called from this repo on real, checksummed sequences and that the results can be filed against a claim with provenance (model, endpoint, version, time, input hashes).

The numbers are consistent with the neutral theory's picture of many substitutions being structurally tolerated: tens of substitutions between orthologs, a predicted fold that superposes within a few angstrom. Consistency is not a test; the claim's status is unchanged by this record.

Both structures in every pair are predictions, so the RMSD measures agreement between model outputs, not experimental truth. Experimental cytochrome c structures exist in the PDB and would be the next comparison.
A real test of the clock claim needs substitution counts against divergence times across many lineages, pre-registered; that is a claim test, not a structure prediction.

claim.statement: Albumin increases the solubility of calcium carbonate and phosphate, whereas its breakdown products dissolve them much less; hence skeletal calcium salts are thrown down when proteins are broken down in metabolism, not by direct action of carbonic acid on a more soluble salt.
claim.quote: The probability is, therefore, that the actual precipitation of the calcium salts is not due to the direct action of carbonic acid, etc. on a more soluble salt (as was at one time believed); but to catabolic changes in the proteids of the organism, which tend to throw down the salts already formed, which had remained hitherto in albuminous solution.

attachments.why_this_protein: Thompson attributes the solubility of skeletal calcium salts to "albuminous solution" and "the proteids of the organism". Serum albumin is the albumin that carries calcium in blood: UniProt annotates it as the major plasma calcium transporter with annotated Ca(2+) binding sites. This record anchors the claim's named substance to a concrete molecule and its predicted structure.

protein.name: Albumin
protein.uniprot_function_annotation: Binds water, Ca(2+), Na(+), K(+), fatty acids, hormones, bilirubin and drugs. Its main function is the regulation of the colloidal osmotic pressure of blood. Major zinc transporter in plasma, typically binds about 80% of all plasma zinc (By similarity). Major calcium and magnesium transporter in plasma, binds approximately 45% of circulating calcium and magnesium in plasma (Probable). Potentially has more than two calcium-binding sites and might additionally bind calcium in a non-specific manner (PubMed:22677715). The shared binding site between zinc and calcium at residue Asp-272 suggests a crosstalk between zinc and calcium transport in the blood (Probable). The rank order of affinity is zinc > calcium > magnesium (Probable). Binds to the bacterial siderophore enterobactin and inhibits enterobactin-mediated iron uptake of E.coli, and may thereby limit the utilization of iron and growth of enteric bacteria such as E.coli (PubMed:6234017). Does not prevent iron uptake by the bacterial siderophore aerobactin (PubMed:6234017)

run.note: NVIDIA_API_KEY is not set in the environment. Nothing was predicted.

what_this_does_and_does_not_show: It shows that a hosted BioNeMo model can be called from this repo on a real, checksummed sequence and that the result can be filed against a claim with provenance (model, endpoint, version, time, input hash).
A predicted structure does not test Thompson's claim about solubility; the claim's status is unchanged by this record.
The next real step would be a pre-registered claim test against solubility measurements, not more structure predictions.
Anything genome-related is out of scope here and would be labelled a sketch.

Present or absent predictions for 12432 species-structure pairs across 48 held-out bird species, made from Uberon taxon constraints alone, with no bird trait data read.
The holdout thread scored the blind Aves predictions inconclusive on all three pre-registered measures (A_keel: inconclusive, B_webbing: inconclusive, C_conflict_free: inconclusive).

ESMFold prediction run for Cytochrome c from Thunnus alalunga (P81459), with its input and output checksums

Pairwise alignment and superposition of the three ESMFold cytochrome c predictions

Across three ESMFold predictions of cytochrome c, the pairs rank the same way by sequence substitutions and by CA RMSD after superposition (Bos taurus vs Thunnus alalunga: 16 substitutions in 103 aligned positions, CA RMSD 0.42 angstrom; Bos taurus vs Saccharomyces cerevisiae (strain ATCC 204508 / S288c): 37 substitutions in 104 aligned positions, CA RMSD 1.67 angstrom; Thunnus alalunga vs Saccharomyces cerevisiae (strain ATCC 204508 / S288c): 38 substitutions in 103 aligned positions, CA RMSD 3.48 angstrom).
